question.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

info.persona: Milagros Coca blends meticulous organization with boundless curiosity, using her garden and kitchen as labs for cultural preservation, though she can’t resist a nightly second cup of oolong tea that keeps her up worrying about upcoming events.
info.professional_persona: Milagros Coca, a retired community organizer turned cultural ambassador, leverages her bilingual fluency, meticulous event‑planning, and deep knowledge of traditional Oaxacan culinary and folk arts to coordinate festivals and mentor younger volunteers, while her innate curiosity drives her to constantly seek new ways to preserve heritage, though she often worries about the details falling short.
info.cultural_background: Milagros was raised in a Mexican‑American household rooted in the traditions of her parents' home region of Oaxaca. She grew up bilingual, celebrating Catholic holidays such as Día de los Muertos, Navidad, and Las Posadas with family rituals, altars, and traditional foods. Community festivals in El Monte, including Cinco de Mayo and local parrilladas, reinforced her connection to Mexican culture while blending Southern Californian influences. Her family places great value on respect for elders, strong family bonds, and community solidarity. These cultural foundations shape her daily life, from cooking authentic dishes to participating in church activities and preserving folk art practices.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Milagros enjoys immersing herself in Mexican culinary arts, experimenting with traditional dishes and sharing meals with family and friends. She spends time crafting embroidered textiles and colorful papel picado for holidays and celebrations. Gardening provides her with a peaceful outlet, where she cultivates herbs, chilies, and tomatoes. She regularly attends local art exhibitions and museum events, especially those featuring Mexican or Latino artists. Reading historical novels and biographies broadens her curiosity about new ideas. Listening to mariachi, Latin jazz, and classic boleros enriches her appreciation for music. Volunteering at the community center keeps her socially engaged, while walking in nearby parks offers quiet reflection. Yoga and meditation help manage stress, and genealogy research connects her to her roots.
info.sports_persona: Milagros Coca enjoys walking the shaded trails of El Monte Community Park, participates in the local senior yoga group, and cheerfully follows the Los Angeles Dodgers and Lakers, balancing relaxed recreation with a commitment to gentle daily movement.
info.arts_persona: Milagros Coca regularly visits the local community arts center to view exhibitions of Frida Kahlo and contemporary muralist Jorge González, devotes afternoons to embroidery while listening to Lila Downs and classic boleros by José José, and volunteers as a docent for a museum’s Latin American art tours, letting her heritage inform her creative practice.
info.travel_persona: Milagros Coca prefers thoughtfully planned itineraries, often organizing family trips that blend cultural immersion with comfortable accommodation; having already explored the historic streets of Oaxaca City and a weekend getaway to Santa Barbara, she now dreams of a pilgrimage to her great‑grandparents’ village in the Sierra Norte while balancing a modest retirement budget.
info.culinary_persona: Milagros Coca, an accomplished home chef, delights in preparing mole negro with toasted chilhuacle peppers, hand‑rolled tamales stuffed with pork and masa, and fresh salsa verde using garden‑grown tomatillos and cilantro, while she balances tradition with occasional daring twists like adding avocado to classic pozole, and she relishes sharing these meals at festive family altars.

info.persona: Juan Collazorivera is a curious, methodical 18‑year‑old whose disciplined compassion drives them to excel in healthcare, guitar, and cooking, even as they juggle a thrifty budget and occasional anxiety about future responsibilities.
info.professional_persona: Juan Collazorivera is a diligent healthcare support worker who blends methodical precision with genuine compassion, leveraging bilingual fluency and keen tech curiosity to excel in vital sign monitoring, EHR documentation, and patient mobility assistance while preparing for CNA certification.
info.cultural_background: Juan is a first‑generation Peruvian‑American. His parents emigrated from Lima in the early 2000s and raised him in a bilingual household in Queens, where Spanish is spoken at home and English at school. He grew up celebrating Peruvian holidays such as Inti Raymi and Día de la Canción Criolla, and his family maintains culinary traditions, often gathering for meals centered on ceviche, causa, and pisco‑based drinks. Catholicism and community ties play a role in his upbringing, and he frequently attends cultural events at the local Peruvian cultural association. At the same time, living in the multicultural environment of Queens has exposed him to a wide range of cultures, shaping a bicultural identity that balances his Peruvian heritage with American life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his downtime Juan enjoys solitary yet enriching activities. He reads science‑fiction and popular‑science books that satisfy his curiosity about technology and the human body. Music is a personal refuge; he practices classical guitar and occasionally plays traditional Andean melodies on a cajón. Cooking is another passion—he perfects dishes like ceviche, lomo saltado, and ají de gallina for family gatherings. Juan also likes hiking in nearby state parks, photographing urban street scenes, and solving puzzles or strategy video games that challenge his methodical mind. Volunteering at the local community center to tutor younger students in Spanish is a way he merges his compassion with his cultural roots.
info.sports_persona: Juan Collazorivera enjoys early‑morning hikes with the Queens Trailblazers club, follows the New York Knicks and New York Mets avidly, and plays casual pickup soccer on weekends at a local community field, treating fitness as a structured yet low‑stress complement to their work schedule.
info.arts_persona: Juan Collazorivera finds solace in practicing classical guitar pieces like Tárrega’s “Recuerdos de la Alhambra,” occasionally drums Andean rhythms on a cajón, and devours science‑fiction novels by Isaac Asimov and Liu Cixin, while also appreciating the cinematic direction of Christopher Nolan and the lyrical storytelling of Lin‑Manuel Miranda.
info.travel_persona: Juan Collazorivera prefers meticulously planned trips that balance adventure and budget, having trekked the Adirondack High Peaks, explored the historic streets of Cartagena, and dreamed of visiting Tokyo for its tech scene and Reykjavik for its stark landscapes, all while keeping travel costs within a part‑time income.
info.culinary_persona: Juan Collazorivera, an intermediate home cook, perfects Peruvian classics like ceviche, lomo saltado, and ají de gallina using ingredients such as fresh lime, aji amarillo, and cilantro, while also experimenting with sushi rolls and homemade gnocchi to broaden their culinary repertoire.

info.persona: Lorraine Damm blends a deep love of nature, disciplined movement, and a relaxed, slightly scattered approach to life, turning solitary hikes into choreography while they juggle a dream studio with a habit of last‑minute planning.
info.professional_persona: Lorraine Damm, a 34‑year‑old choreographer and movement educator based in Bozeman, blends contemporary and ballet techniques with improvisational site‑specific work, leverages Laban movement notation and a deep humanities grounding to craft environmentally themed pieces, and they embrace a relaxed, flexible workflow that values curiosity over strict scheduling while fostering inclusive community workshops.
info.cultural_background: Lorraine grew up in a middle‑class white family in the Midwest before moving to Bozeman to pursue her artistic career. Her upbringing included exposure to classic American modern dance pioneers such as Martha Graham and Merce Cunningham, which shaped her appreciation for expressive movement. Living in Montana has deepened her connection to the region's rugged landscapes and close‑knit community values. While she acknowledges the area's Indigenous heritage, she actively seeks respectful collaborations with local Native artists and incorporates culturally aware narratives into her work. Her humanities education reinforces a broad, interdisciplinary outlook that blends European artistic traditions with the distinctive ethos of the American West.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime, Lorraine frequents the nearby mountains for solo hikes, drawing inspiration from the sweeping vistas for her choreography. She enjoys nature photography, capturing movement in light and weather. A lover of quiet creativity, she practices yoga and meditation to maintain physical and emotional balance. Lorraine also dives into literary nonfiction and poetry from her humanities studies, often reading works on philosophy and cultural theory. She experiments with costume design, hand‑sewing fabrics for her performances, and attends local film screenings and contemporary art exhibitions to stay abreast of new creative ideas.
info.sports_persona: Lorraine Damm, an avid solo hiker, spends weekends traversing the Bridger Mountains, follows the Montana State Bobcats football team, trains with the Bozeman Trail Running Club in spring, and they balance winter fitness with snowshoeing, yoga, and occasional viewings of Colorado Avalanche games.
info.arts_persona: Lorraine Damm cultivates a vibrant artistic life, capturing movement‑inspired landscapes through photography, hand‑sewing costumes reminiscent of Olafur Eliasson’s color palettes, attending Chantal Akerman film screenings, and they draw choreographic inspiration from Merce Cunningham, William Forsythe, and the poetry of Ocean Vuong.
info.travel_persona: Lorraine Damm prefers unstructured, eco‑focused travel, often planning spontaneous week‑long hikes in Banff National Park, dreaming of a residency in Wuppertal, Germany’s Pina Bausch Archive, and they seek reflective retreats among Sedona’s red‑rock canyons whenever time and budget allow.
info.culinary_persona: Lorraine Damm enjoys cooking wholesome, locally sourced meals such as rosemary‑infused bison stew, wild mushroom risotto, and sourdough topped with honey‑lavender glaze, yet they often forget pantry staples, leading to spontaneous foraging trips for fresh herbs and forest mushrooms.
